chain.title: Give Bulk Materials a Home
chain.desc: Make a drawer and insert a material you collect in quantity. Its front is the interface for depositing and removing items.

chain.title: Split a Storage Block
chain.desc: Try a two-compartment drawer for paired materials. Each compartment keeps its own item assignment and shares the block's available capacity.

chain.title: Keep the Assignments Stable
chain.desc: Use a Drawer Key to lock item assignments. Locked empty drawers can retain the intended item type, which helps automated storage stay organized.

chain.title: Plan the Capacity Upgrades
chain.desc: Craft an Upgrade Template for specialized upgrades. Capacity tiers are alternatives; every earlier tier need not be crafted to use a later one.

chain.title: More Room for Everyday Materials
chain.desc: Install an Iron Storage Upgrade in a busy drawer and check its displayed capacity. Keep automation below the new limit or provide overflow handling.

chain.title: Reserve Deep Storage for the Busiest Lines
chain.desc: Use a Diamond Storage Upgrade for high-volume resources. Choose the drawers that actually need it instead of upgrading the entire wall blindly.

chain.title: Deliberate Overflow Handling
chain.desc: Install a Void Upgrade only where losing excess items is acceptable. It disposes of overflow; it does not provide extra recoverable storage.

chain.title: One Resource in Several Forms
chain.desc: Insert a resource with a supported compacting recipe. The drawer exposes related block, ingot or nugget forms from the same stored quantity.

chain.title: One Access Point for the Wall
chain.desc: Build a Drawer Controller and connect it to your drawer network. Feed bulk materials through the controller instead of piping to each drawer separately.

chain.title: Bridge the Gaps
chain.desc: Use trim to connect drawer sections where you do not need another inventory. Keep the layout within the installed controller's range rules.

chain.title: Another Connection to the Same Store
chain.desc: Add a Controller Slave or Controller IO as an extra automation access point. It serves the connected network rather than creating a separate store.

chain.title: Make Stock Levels Visible
chain.desc: Use the Quantify Key to toggle visible item counts. Read the wall at a glance before scaling up a farm.

chain.title: Test the Entire Storage Route
chain.desc: Insert several assigned materials through the controller and extract them again through the network. Confirm once every material reaches the correct locked drawer.

chain.title: Store a Farm's Real Output
chain.desc: Connect an actual farm or processing line and watch repeated output arrive. Confirm after handling any secondary drops and choosing an intentional overflow policy.

content_revision: 2026-10-07: explicit branches, operational guidance, no collection filler

coverage.scope: Lockable bulk storage, capacity and compacting branches, connected controllers, and tested farm output.
coverage.limitations: Recipe quantities, enabled content and progression settings may be changed by the installed pack.
coverage.verification_detail: Item models, entity language identifiers, dimension data, recipes and bundled guide text where present were inspected; this is data verification, not a Minecraft playthrough.

notes: Each requires list is intentional. Empty lists are independent entry routes. Links describe guided progression or demonstrated recipe/boss gates, not an assertion that every dependency is a game-enforced lock. Runtime scanning still filters unavailable items and entities.
